chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Bakr ibn Isa ibn Ahmad al-Alawi, who said:

I was in the mosque when a funeral was brought, and I intended to pray over it. Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) came, placed his elbow on my chest, and kept pushing me until he took me out of the mosque. Then he said, 'O Abu Bakr, indeed funerals are not prayed over in the mosques.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلُ: Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (Imam Hasan al-Askari, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Where should funeral prayers be performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic preference (or prohibition, depending on the school of thought) against performing funeral prayers within the main prayer halls of mosques, a ruling attributed to Imam al-Hasan al-Awwa (peace be upon him). The physical gesture of the Imam pushing the narrator out serves as a practical demonstration of this distinction between the sanctity of daily congregational prayer and the specific protocol for funeral rites. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the Imams' specific procedural guidelines regarding ritual purity and spatial sanctity in worship.
